title: Protocol for tissue slice cultures from human solid tumors to study therapeutic response
protocol: Collect human tissue in a sterile manner.
Remove a wedge of tumor tissue approximately 1 cm thick from the specimen under pathologist guidance using sterile surgical tools.
Use a 6 mm biopsy punch to core the tumor tissue for further processing.
Ensure the presence of a pathology representative during tissue collection.
Use a 6-mm biopsy punch to obtain cores of tumor tissue from the wedge.
Place tumor tissue cores directly in 3 mL of ice-cold Belzer UW Cold Storage Solution in 5 mL Eppendorf tubes (sterile).
Maintain samples on ice and transport them immediately to the research lab.
Take tissue cores from the periphery of the tumor to avoid areas of central necrosis.
Keep the time between surgical resection completion and tissue procurement under 10 minutes.
If the time exceeds 45 minutes, test tissue viability before proceeding with experiments.
Transport procured tissue on ice immediately to the research lab for precision cut slice generation.
Remove tissue cores from UW solution using sterile forceps.
Place tissue cores in a sterile petri dish.
Dab excess liquid on sterile gauze.
Embed cores in 2% agarose for slicing.
Position individual cores in the center of one well of a sterile 24-well plate.
Pipette warm (37°C), 2% agarose solution over top of core(s) until tissue is entirely covered.
Cover the plate and place it on ice.
Agarose should solidify in 5 min.
Cut along the edge of the agarose in the well using a sterile scalpel or spatula.
Pop the embedded tissue out of the well and onto a sterile petri dish.
Glue the face of the embedded core that was on the bottom of the well directly to the specimen disc with superglue.
Place the buffer tray in an ice holder and cover it.
Add ice around the buffer tray.
Fill the buffer tray with ice-cold cutting buffer.
Slide the ice tray onto the vibratome stand and lock it in place by moving the lever to the right.
Secure blade into blade holder with an Allen wrench.
Rotate the blade into cutting position using the Allen wrench.
Raise the stage up using the control pad until the blade touches the liquid in the buffer tray.
Set cutting window using the control pad.
Step down 250 μm at a time at 1.5 mm/s until the blade reaches the tallest tissue core.
Adjust settings on the vibratome depending on the consistency and integrity of the tissue and the number of cores being sliced (amplitude 2–3, speed 0.5–1.5 mm/s).
Gently scoop out uniform 250 μm slices from the bath using sterile spatula or forceps.
Place each slice in one well of a 48-well dish containing prewarmed modified WME or media of choice.
Transfer slices onto individual Millicell culture inserts placed in a 24-well plate.
Place 450 μL of media in each well containing the culture inserts.
Plate one tumor slice on a 12 mm insert in a 24-well dish.
Plate four tumor slices on a 30 mm insert in a 6-well dish.
Incubate plates with slices on a rocker at 37°C and approximately 20 rocks per minute for 1 to 4 hours for washing.
Assess tissue viability on a small sample of slices before experiments commence.
Place one Millicell cell culture insert into each well of a 24-well tissue culture plate using sterile forceps.
Pipette 450 μL of growth media, modified William’s media E supplemented with hEGF (20 ng/mL), into each well.
Plate tissue slices on cell culture inserts to maintain viability.
Transfer one slice into each insert using a pipette tip or sterile forceps.
Use the liquid in the insert to help remove the slice from the transfer tool.
Gently move the floating slice with a pipette tip to ensure it is completely flat.
Remove media in the insert to the outside to prevent folding of the slice.
Rock plate containing slices at 20 rocks/min, 37°C and 5% CO2 to expose tissue interface to media and air intermittently.
Thaw 5 mL aliquots of CellTiter 96 AQueous One Solution (MTS reagent) in 37°C water bath.
Place 400 μL of media into each well of a 48-well dish.
Transfer slices from the Millicell insert to individual wells.
Keep track of slice identification number.
Maintain 3 wells without slices as blanks.
Add 80 μL of MTS reagent to each well of the plate.
Incubate tissue with MTS reagent for approximately 3 hours.
Transfer 200 μL of each blank well and each slice well to a 96-well assay plate after incubation.
Read absorbance at 490 nm.
Keep track of every slice when moving from insert to 48-well dish for MTS.
Incubate tumor slices for 12 to 18 hours.
Treat slices with chemotherapy or immunotherapy as needed, timing treatment between 2 and 6 days.
Perform pre-treatment MTS on half of the slices before plating to determine change in viability with treatment.
Treat tumor slices from CRLM with vehicle control (0.2% DMSO), FX (1 μg/mL 5FU + 1 μg/mL Oxaliplatin), FI (1 μg/mL 5FU + 2 μg/mL Irinotecan), or STS (10 μm Staurosporine) two times over 4 days.
Use treated slices to calculate percent change in viability using pre-treatment and post-treatment MTS values.
Subsequently fix the slices for histology after treatment.
Process fixed slices for immunohistochemistry staining with Ki67.
Prepare working solutions of chemotherapies or immunotherapies by diluting stock solutions of each drug in media the following day.
Incubate tissue slices at 37°C and 5% CO2 with chemotherapy or immunotherapy for desired treatment period.
Add fresh drug every 1 to 2 days depending on treatment duration.
Treat slices with immunotherapies or combined chemo-immunotherapies as appropriate.
Perform downstream assays at the end of the treatment.
Calculate percent change in viability using the equation ((post-treatment MTS – pre-treatment MTS) / pre-treatment MTS Absorbance) * 100.
Average percent change in viability for each treatment group.
Place additional treated slices in RNAlater for RNAseq analysis.
Keep track of the identification number and corresponding treatment group for each slice.
Fix slices exposed to MTS reagent for histological analysis or freeze them for protein analysis, such as Western Blot.
Do not expose slices intended for RNA analysis or live imaging to MTS reagent.
Prepare parallel treatment replicates for slices used in RNA analysis or live imaging.
Prepare GEMs or CAR-T cells as described in previously published work.
Thaw frozen aliquots of CAR-T cells at the time of the experiment if used instead of GEMs.
Incubate tumor slices for 12 – 18 hours after preparation.
Stain GEMs or CAR-T cells with Carboxyfluorescein succinimidyl ester (CFSE) according to manufacturer’s protocols.
Resuspend stained cells in cell culture media to a predetermined cell number and concentration desired for the experiment.
Remove previously untreated slice culture media from slices.
Replace removed media with 400 μl of fresh slice culture media containing any additional treatment or controls at appropriate concentrations.
Add cellular therapy to each slice to achieve a final volume of 450 μl.
Incubate slices with GEMs or CAR-T cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for the desired treatment period.
Fix slices in formalin for histology and immunohistochemistry four and seven days after GEM addition.
Store fixed slices in RNAlater for transcriptomic analyses.
Perform live cell imaging on slices as needed.
Stain adaptive cellular therapy with CFSE for imaging.
Use fluorescently labeled antibodies to stain and identify tumor cells expressing EpCAM antigen.
Label apoptotic cells with SR-FLICA reagent.
Transfer tumor slices to a 48-well plate containing 500 μL of fresh media with 10 μg/mL Alexa 647 EpCAM antibody and SR-FLICA reagent.
Incubate the slices for 3 h at 37°C.
Stain the nuclei using 10 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 for 10 min.
Wash the slices of fluorescent staining antibodies by transferring them twice to separate wells containing PBS.
Return the slices with their original media containing the treatment to an 8-well chamber slide with a coverslip bottom for imaging.
Maintain tissue slices at 37°C using a covered stage while flushing with warmed, humidified CO2.
Image the slices using a confocal microscope at 20× magnification.
Imaging duration is for 1 hour at multiple positions within each slice with a z-stack of 20 μm.
Perform image processing and data analysis on Leica LAS X software.
Use Imaris software to count apoptotic tumor cells that are EpCAM+ SR-FLICA+ and CFSE+ CAR-T cells.
Utilize Imaris for proximity analysis among other analyses.
